name: Big dirty bulk (Fast-food bulking)

lead: A big dirty bulk means eating a very large calorie surplus without careful tracking, often from fast food, to gain mass quickly and cut the fat afterward. Proponents find it simpler than strict meal planning.

A large surplus supplies energy for muscle growth, with the excess stored as fat. Bodybuilding references say it can speed muscle and strength gains but usually adds significant body fat; no clinical studies of fast-food bulking for appearance were found.

paras: People combine lifting with calorie-dense convenience foods and little macro tracking, then follow with a harder cut. It contrasts with a clean bulk that aims to add muscle with little fat.
Added body fat requires a harder cut afterward, and reference sources mention possible effects on heart health and insulin sensitivity.

angle.text: Users eat a very large surplus of calorie-dense fast food to gain mass quickly, planning to cut fat afterward. Lifters report faster scale gains; comparisons with cleaner bulks come mostly from lifter experience.

lead: A dirty bulk is a weight-gain approach in which a person eats a large calorie surplus without carefully tracking macronutrients, often using calorie-dense convenience or fast food. Lifters use it to put on size and strength quickly in the off-season, then diet the extra fat off. It contrasts with a "clean bulk" that aims to gain muscle with little fat.[1]

Bodybuilding reference material says dirty bulking can produce quick muscle and strength gains but usually adds significant body fat, requiring a harder cut afterward, and mentions possible effects on cardiovascular health and insulin sensitivity over time. It also notes some lifters find it psychologically easier because it avoids strict meal planning and tracking.[1]

On T Nation and looksmax.org the topic is a long-running debate. Some lifters report being glad they dirty bulked, while others advise a cleaner approach, especially for people not using anabolic drugs.[2][3][4] No clinical studies of fast-food bulking for appearance were found.

paras: Bulking means eating in a calorie surplus to keep the body in a growth-supporting state, and a larger surplus or longer bulk adds more body fat, according to bodybuilding references, which describe cutting as the later calorie-deficit phase for losing it.[1] Clean bulking involves hitting calorie targets daily with tracked food, while dirty bulking skips close tracking and often leans on junk food.[1]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and lifting communities
paras: On looksmax.org, a skinny poster asking whether to clean or dirty bulk received replies that clean bulking is better, one reply adding that dirty bulking is better suited to people using steroids.[2] In another thread a user told a 16-year-old that clean is "obviously better" than dirty.[3]

A long-running T Nation thread titled "I'm Happy That I Dirty Bulked" shows the other side. The original poster described going from about 210 lb at 15 percent body fat to 252 lb at 17 percent over roughly a year, with large strength gains, and then dieting down. Replies argued that timing heavier meals around training may limit fat gain, that muscle gain matters more than a body-fat figure, and that "dirty" has no fixed definition. Other posters cautioned that poorly planned bulks with weak training or low protein add fat with little benefit.[4]

Reference material lists added body fat that requires a harder cut, and possible effects on cardiovascular health and insulin sensitivity over time.[1] It also notes that it is unclear whether enough lean mass can be kept through cutting for the whole cycle to be worthwhile.[1]

lore.intro: Dirty versus clean bulking is a recurring argument in lifting forums, with no agreed definition of how dirty a bulk is.[2][4]

claims.claim: A dirty bulk builds size and strength faster than a clean bulk.
Dirty bulking is better suited to people using steroids.
The fat gained will be a burden to cut afterward.
